# Notification centre

The record of what happened: a bell with an unread count, and the notifications under it, kept after their toasts have gone.

Status: Experimental. Its API may change in a minor release, without a deprecation first.

Where a notification goes after its toast has gone. **The toast is the moment, the centre is the record**: the same event usually goes to both, the toast to say it now and the centre to find it later. The centre never says it now: no live region, and the unread count changes silently, because the toast already announced the event. The count is in the bell’s name, “Notifications, 2 unread”, heard when someone goes to the bell. Unread is an ink edge, a semibold title and the word New, never a tint alone. The list is a prop: the page owns where notifications come from and whether “read” is saved.

## Usage

### When to use

- Events the operator may have missed: a failed run, an approval waiting, a view shared with them.
- The other half of a toast: send the same event to both, the toast to say it now and the centre to find it later.
- A full notifications page, with NotificationList on its own.

### When not to

- Saying an event now, where the operator is looking. Use [Toast](https://demogar.github.io/molaui/md/components-feedback-toast--overview.md).
- A condition of the whole application that is still true. Use [Banner](https://demogar.github.io/molaui/md/components-feedback-banner--overview.md).
- The history of one object, such as a run’s steps or a deploy log. Use [Timeline](https://demogar.github.io/molaui/md/components-data-display-timeline--overview.md).

### Do and don’t

- Do: Add the event to the centre when you raise its toast.
- Don’t: Raise a toast for an event that matters later and keep no record of it.
- Do: Let the unread count change silently; the bell’s name carries it.
- Don’t: Announce each new notification from the centre as well; the toast already said it.

### Content

- The title says what happened, in the past tense, standing on its own: “Re-index failed for Billing FAQ”.
- Times are relative while recent, “4 min ago”, and absolute after a day, “Yesterday 16:20”.
- The action is one verb: “View run”, “Review”.

## Anatomy

The root carries `data-slot="notification-list"`; each part carries its `data-part`.

1. Notification (`[data-part="item"]`): One event. Unread, it carries a heavy ink edge at its start.
2. Tone mark (`[data-part="tone"]`): The toast’s own cut square, so the record is recognisably the toast it came from.
3. Title (`[data-part="title"]`): What happened, in the past tense; semibold while unread.
4. New (`[data-part="unread"]`): The word that says unread, beside the edge and the weight, so unread is never colour alone.
5. Time (`[data-part="time"]`): When, as a person reads it, in a time element with the machine date.
6. Action (`[data-part="action"]`): One follow-up; running it marks the notification read.

## API

### `NotificationCentre` (component)

The bell for the top bar's `end`, and the list in a popover under it. `className`, `ref` and the rest go to the popover popup.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `notifications` (required) | `NotificationItem[]` |  | Newest first. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | Open on first render. |
| `empty` | `ReactNode` |  | Shown when there is nothing. Defaults to “No notifications yet.” (`messages.empty`) |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` |  | Under the list: usually a link to a full notifications page, “View all”. |
| `label` | `string` |  | The popover's title and the bell's name, “Notifications” (`messages.label`) by default. |
| `messages` | `MessagesOverride<NotificationsMessages>` |  | Words for translation: the defaults above, the unread and tone words, Mark all as read and the bell's name. Keys left out come from `MessagesProvider`, then English. |
| `onMarkAllRead` | `(() => void)` |  | Called when the operator presses Mark all as read. The button shows only while something is unread. |
| `onMarkRead` | `((id: string) => void)` |  | Called with an item's id when its action runs. |
| `onOpenChange` | `((open: boolean) => void)` |  | Called when the popover opens or closes. |
| `open` | `boolean` |  | Whether the popover is open, when the page owns that. |

`className`, `ref`, `id` and the other DOM props go to `<div data-slot="notification-centre">`.

### `NotificationList` (component)

The list on its own, for a full notifications page or a panel the page places itself. `NotificationCentre` puts it in a popover under a bell. `className`, `ref` and the rest go to the wrapping `<div>`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `notifications` (required) | `NotificationItem[]` |  | Newest first. |
| `empty` | `ReactNode` |  | Shown when there is nothing. Defaults to “No notifications yet.” (`messages.empty`) |
| `label` | `string` |  | The list's accessible name, “Notifications” (`messages.label`) by default. |
| `messages` | `MessagesOverride<NotificationsMessages>` |  | Words for translation: the defaults above, the unread and tone words, Mark all as read and the bell's name. Keys left out come from `MessagesProvider`, then English. |
| `onMarkRead` | `((id: string) => void)` |  | Called with an item's id when its action runs. |

`className`, `ref`, `id` and the other DOM props go to `<div data-slot="notification-list">`.

Types: `NotificationsMessages`, `NotificationCentreProps`, `NotificationItem`, `NotificationListProps`, `NotificationTone`

## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Enter or Space | On the bell, opens the list and moves focus into it. |
| Tab or Shift+Tab | Moves through Mark all as read and each notification’s action. |
| Escape | Closes the list and returns focus to the bell. |

### Mola handles

- Names the bell “Notifications”, with the unread count when there is one: “Notifications, 2 unread”.
- Changes the count silently, with no live region: the toast that raised the event already announced it.
- Renders a named list; each unread item starts with a hidden “Unread.” and its tone in words.
- Shows unread as an ink edge, a semibold title and the word New, never colour alone.
- Keeps focus in the popover when Mark all as read, its own button, goes away.

### You handle

- Raise a toast for an event that needs saying now; the centre will not say it.
- Write titles that stand on their own, away from the page they came from.
- Save the read state if it should survive a reload.

### Testing status

- Automated, jsdom: each of its 6 stories is rendered and checked with axe on every pull request.
- Automated, browser: every story is checked in Chromium with axe, colour contrast included, in both themes, and for overflow at 390px.
- Keyboard in unit tests: yes, every key in the table is pressed.
- Screen readers: not yet tested by hand.
